trials.name: NSABP B-06
trials.result: No OS difference at 20 y; ipsilateral recurrence 39.2% without RT vs 14.3% with RT
trials.takeaway: Breast-conserving surgery + RT is equivalent to mastectomy; RT is essential after lumpectomy.

inclusion: Stage I–II invasive breast cancer, tumour ≤4 cm
strengths: Three-arm design isolated the effect of RT after lumpectomy
limitations: Pre-dates modern imaging, systemic therapy and margin standards
Data-integrity scandal at one site (reanalysis confirmed results)
appraisal.critique: Foundational proof that breast conservation plus RT is equivalent to mastectomy for survival. Absolute recurrence rates without RT are far higher than in today's well-staged, systemically treated patients, so the size of the RT benefit is overstated for modern practice.

trials.name: Milan I (Veronesi)
trials.takeaway: Quadrantectomy + RT is a safe alternative to mastectomy for small cancers.

limitations: Quadrantectomy is more extensive than modern lumpectomy
No systemic therapy for node-negative patients
appraisal.critique: Together with B-06 it established breast conservation. Results apply to small tumours; the extensive quadrantectomy and boost used make it less directly comparable with today's margin-directed lumpectomy.

trials.name: EBCTCG RT overview
trials.result: 10-y any recurrence 19.3% vs 35.0%; 15-y BC death 21.4% vs 25.2%
trials.takeaway: RT after BCS halves recurrence; roughly one BC death avoided per four recurrences prevented.

inclusion: Randomised trials of RT vs no RT after breast-conserving surgery
Women with invasive breast cancer, pN0 or pN+
strengths: Individual patient-level meta-analysis — highest level of evidence
Links recurrence reduction to mortality benefit (~1 death avoided per 4 recurrences prevented)
limitations: Many trials used old RT techniques and no modern systemic therapy
Heterogeneous surgery, margins and RT doses
Cannot identify subgroups who safely omit RT in modern era
appraisal.critique: Robust demonstration that local control matters for survival. Absolute benefits in modern low-risk patients on endocrine therapy are smaller, which is why omission trials (PRIME II, CALGB 9343) followed.

trials.name: START-B
trials.result: 10-y LRR 5.5% (50 Gy) vs 4.3% (40 Gy); fewer late normal-tissue effects with 40 Gy
trials.takeaway: Moderate hypofractionation (40 Gy/15) became standard whole-breast RT.

inclusion: Women with early invasive breast cancer (pT1–3a, pN0–1)
exclusion: Need for nodal RT in most protocols (allowed but uncommon)
strengths: Large, multicentre, pragmatic trial with 10-year follow-up
Measured photographic and patient-reported late effects
limitations: Limited data for nodal RT and reconstruction
appraisal.critique: Practice-changing: 40 Gy/15 is at least as effective with fewer late effects than 50 Gy/25. Applicability to nodal RT and reconstruction relied on later trials.

trials.name: FAST-Forward
trials.result: 5-y IBTR 2.1% (40 Gy) vs 1.7% (27 Gy) vs 1.4% (26 Gy); 26 Gy non-inferior with similar normal-tissue effects
trials.takeaway: 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week is a standard option for whole-breast/chest-wall RT.

inclusion: Invasive breast cancer pT1–3, pN0–1, M0
strengths: Detailed clinician, patient and photographic normal-tissue assessment
limitations: Low event rate — non-inferiority margins applied to small absolute numbers
Limited data on boost, nodal RT and reconstruction
appraisal.critique: Shows 26 Gy/5 fractions is non-inferior with similar toxicity, saving 2 weeks of travel — highly relevant in India. Concerns remain about generalising to nodal RT, reconstruction and large breasts.

trials.name: EORTC 22881 Boost
trials.result: 20-y IBTR 12.0% vs 16.4% (HR 0.65); largest absolute benefit in age ≤40
trials.takeaway: Boost reduces local recurrence, especially in younger women; no OS benefit.

inclusion: Stage I–II breast cancer after lumpectomy with microscopically complete excision
limitations: Pre-dates modern margins and systemic therapy
appraisal.critique: Boost roughly halves local recurrence relative risk but the absolute gain is small in older women; it supports selective boosting (young age, high grade) rather than boosting everyone.

trials.name: MA.20
trials.population: Node-positive or high-risk node-negative after BCS
trials.result: 10-y DFS 82.0% vs 77.0% (HR 0.76); OS not significantly different
trials.takeaway: Regional nodal RT improves DFS in node-positive disease.

inclusion: Adjuvant chemotherapy and/or endocrine therapy as indicated
strengths: Randomised evidence for regional nodal irradiation
appraisal.critique: Regional nodal RT improved disease-free survival but not OS. Its main value is in reducing regional and distant recurrence, which must be balanced against lymphoedema and lung toxicity.

trials.name: EORTC 22922
trials.result: 10-y OS 82.3% vs 80.7% (NS at 10 y); reduced BC mortality on 15-y update
trials.takeaway: Supports internal mammary/supraclavicular RT in higher-risk disease.

inclusion: Medial/central tumours or axillary node involvement
limitations: OS benefit modest and not statistically significant at 10 years
Older RT techniques with possible cardiac dose
appraisal.critique: Supports IMN-medial supraclavicular RT for high-risk patients. Benefits are small and must be weighed against cardiac dose, especially with left-sided tumours.

trials.name: Danish 82b/82c & EBCTCG PMRT
trials.result: EBCTCG (1–3 nodes): 20-y BC mortality reduced 7.9% absolute with PMRT
trials.takeaway: PMRT reduces recurrence and BC mortality even with 1–3 positive nodes.

inclusion: High-risk: node-positive, tumour >5 cm or skin/fascia invasion
Pre- (82b, with CMF) or postmenopausal (82c, with tamoxifen)
strengths: Showed overall survival benefit from post-mastectomy RT
Confirmed by EBCTCG meta-analysis even for 1–3 positive nodes
limitations: Inadequate axillary dissection (median ~7 nodes) inflated regional recurrence
appraisal.critique: Practice-defining for PMRT, but the high locoregional recurrence in controls partly reflected limited axillary surgery. In 1–3 node-positive disease today the absolute gain is smaller.

trials.name: CALGB 9343
trials.result: 10-y local recurrence 2% vs 10%; no OS difference
trials.takeaway: RT omission is reasonable in older women with small ER+ tumours on endocrine therapy.

strengths: Showed no survival effect of omitting RT in older women
limitations: Many deaths from other causes limit power
Adherence to tamoxifen not well documented
appraisal.critique: Supports omitting RT in women ≥70 with small ER+ tumours who take endocrine therapy. The key trade-off is that local recurrence is higher, and stopping endocrine therapy removes the safety net.

trials.name: PRIME II
trials.population: Age ≥65, HR+, node-negative, ≤3 cm, on endocrine therapy
trials.takeaway: Omitting RT is an option in low-risk older women willing to take endocrine therapy.

inclusion: Clear margins (≥1 mm), on adjuvant endocrine therapy
strengths: Large randomised omission trial with 10-year results
Clear absolute risk numbers for shared decisions
limitations: Low event rate limits power for subgroups
Most deaths unrelated to breast cancer
appraisal.critique: Omitting RT raises 10-year local recurrence from about 1% to 9% with no survival difference. A strong basis for shared decision-making in older women, but it depends on endocrine adherence.

trials.name: NSABP B-39/RTOG 0413
trials.result: 10-y IBTR 4.6% vs 3.9%; did not meet equivalence criteria
trials.takeaway: APBI is acceptable for carefully selected low-risk patients; WBRT remains the reference.

inclusion: Stage 0–II (≤3 cm, ≤3 positive nodes) after lumpectomy
limitations: APBI did not meet equivalence criteria
Mixed risk population including higher-risk patients
appraisal.critique: Ipsilateral recurrence was only slightly higher with APBI, but the trial failed formal equivalence. It supports APBI for carefully selected low-risk women rather than broad use.

trials.name: IMPORT LOW
trials.result: 5-y local relapse 1.1% (WB) vs 0.5% (partial); partial-breast non-inferior with fewer late effects
trials.takeaway: External-beam partial-breast RT is a standard option for low-risk disease.

inclusion: Invasive ductal carcinoma, pT1–2 (≤3 cm), pN0–1
strengths: Simple IMRT-based partial-breast technique, easy to deliver
Non-inferiority shown with fewer adverse effects
appraisal.critique: Partial-breast RT with standard external beam is non-inferior to whole-breast RT for low-risk women and reduces breast changes — a practical, easily adopted approach.

trials.name: ACOSOG Z0011
trials.population: T1–2, cN0, 1–2 positive SLNs, BCS + WBRT
trials.result: 10-y OS 86.3% vs 83.6% (non-inferior); regional recurrence <2% both arms
trials.takeaway: ALND can be omitted with 1–2 positive sentinel nodes treated with BCS + whole-breast RT.

inclusion: Breast-conserving surgery with planned whole-breast RT
exclusion: ≥3 positive sentinel nodes or matted nodes
limitations: Closed early due to poor accrual and low event rate (n=891 vs planned 1,900)
Unknown nodal RT fields — 'high tangents' were often used
appraisal.critique: Omitting axillary dissection is safe in this narrow group, but the trial was underpowered and RT fields were not controlled. It should not be extrapolated to mastectomy or neoadjuvant settings.

trials.name: AMAROS
trials.result: Axillary recurrence very low in both (≈1%); lymphoedema roughly halved with RT
trials.takeaway: Axillary RT is an alternative to ALND with less lymphoedema.

strengths: Showed less lymphoedema with axillary RT
limitations: Low axillary event rate made non-inferiority test underpowered
appraisal.critique: Axillary RT gives similar regional control with about half the lymphoedema of dissection. It is a reasonable alternative where dissection would otherwise be done.

trials.name: SOUND
trials.population: Tumour ≤2 cm, negative axillary ultrasound, BCS
trials.takeaway: Axillary surgery can be omitted in selected small tumours with negative ultrasound.

strengths: Tests complete omission of axillary surgery
limitations: Loss of nodal staging information may affect systemic therapy decisions (e.g. CDK4/6i)
appraisal.critique: Supports omitting SLNB in low-risk older women with negative ultrasound. Loss of nodal information is a real downside now that nodal status determines adjuvant abemaciclib or ribociclib.

trials.name: Oxford Overview (EBCTCG) chemo
trials.result: Taxane-plus-anthracycline regimens reduce BC mortality by about one-third vs no chemo
trials.takeaway: Benefit of modern chemo is proportional and largely independent of age, ER and nodal status.

strengths: Highest level of evidence, individual patient data
Shows proportional benefit largely independent of age, nodal status and ER
limitations: Proportional benefit does not translate into similar absolute benefit for low-risk patients
appraisal.critique: Taxane-anthracycline regimens reduce breast cancer mortality by about a third. Absolute benefit depends on baseline risk, which is why genomic assays now guide chemotherapy.

trials.name: CALGB 9741
trials.takeaway: Established dose-dense AC→paclitaxel with G-CSF.

strengths: 2×2 factorial design tested both dose density and sequence
limitations: Benefit seen mainly in ER-negative disease
appraisal.critique: Dose-dense every-2-week AC→T improved DFS and OS. Gains were concentrated in ER-negative tumours, so the benefit for ER-positive disease is debated.

trials.name: E1199
trials.population: Node-positive or high-risk N0 after AC
trials.result: Weekly paclitaxel and q3w docetaxel superior to q3w paclitaxel (DFS HR ≈0.84)
trials.takeaway: Weekly paclitaxel after AC became a standard taxane schedule.

inclusion: Node-positive or high-risk node-negative operable breast cancer
limitations: HER2+ patients included before trastuzumab era
appraisal.critique: Weekly paclitaxel and 3-weekly docetaxel were superior to 3-weekly paclitaxel. Weekly paclitaxel became the preferred taxane, with particular benefit in TNBC.

trials.name: TAILORx
trials.result: 9-y IDFS 83.3% vs 84.3% (HR 1.08, non-inferior); some benefit of chemo age ≤50 with RS 16–25
trials.takeaway: Most node-negative patients with RS ≤25 can skip chemotherapy.

limitations: Exploratory finding of some chemo benefit in women ≤50 with RS 16–25 (possibly ovarian suppression effect)
Clinical risk not used for randomisation
appraisal.critique: Most women with RS ≤25 can skip chemotherapy. The benefit seen in younger women may reflect chemotherapy-induced ovarian suppression rather than cytotoxic effect.

trials.name: RxPONDER
trials.result: Postmenopausal: no chemo benefit; premenopausal: 5-y IDFS 94.2% vs 89.0%
trials.takeaway: Postmenopausal N1 with RS ≤25 can omit chemo; premenopausal still benefit.

limitations: Ovarian suppression rarely used in premenopausal women
appraisal.critique: Postmenopausal women with 1–3 nodes and RS ≤25 can skip chemotherapy. Premenopausal women benefited, raising the question whether ovarian suppression could substitute for chemotherapy.

trials.name: MINDACT
trials.population: Early BC, high clinical but low genomic (MammaPrint) risk
trials.result: 5-y DMFS 94.7% without chemo (met prespecified threshold); ~1.5% absolute benefit with chemo
trials.takeaway: MammaPrint low-risk can spare about 46% of clinically high-risk patients from chemo.

inclusion: Discordant clinical (Adjuvant! Online) and genomic (MammaPrint) risk randomised
strengths: Prospective validation of a genomic signature
limitations: Primary endpoint tested only in chemo-omitted arm (single-arm comparison to threshold)
About 1.5% absolute DMFS benefit with chemo was not ruled out
Benefit with chemo seen in women ≤50
appraisal.critique: Supports omitting chemotherapy for high clinical/low genomic risk postmenopausal women. The small absolute benefit seen with chemotherapy in younger women needs individual discussion.

trials.name: ATAC
trials.takeaway: Aromatase inhibitors are preferred adjuvant ET in postmenopausal women.

limitations: Combination arm closed for lack of benefit
appraisal.critique: Anastrozole improved recurrence outcomes and reduced endometrial cancer and VTE versus tamoxifen, at the cost of fractures and arthralgia. OS was unchanged.

trials.name: ATLAS / aTTom
trials.takeaway: Extended tamoxifen (10 y) reduces recurrence and mortality.

strengths: Very large trials with long follow-up
limitations: Excess endometrial cancer and pulmonary embolism
Largely pre-AI era; many patients today take AIs
appraisal.critique: Ten years of tamoxifen lowers recurrence and breast cancer mortality, with benefits emerging late. It is mainly relevant for premenopausal women who cannot take AIs.

trials.name: SOFT / TEXT
trials.result: Exemestane + OFS best; benefit concentrated in high-risk (young, chemo-treated) patients; OS gain in SOFT high-risk
trials.takeaway: Add ovarian suppression for higher-risk premenopausal women.

inclusion: Premenopausal women with HR-positive early breast cancer
strengths: Identified high-risk groups benefiting from OFS
limitations: More menopausal symptoms, sexual dysfunction and bone loss
Benefit mostly in women who needed chemotherapy and remained premenopausal
appraisal.critique: Ovarian suppression plus exemestane improves outcomes for higher-risk premenopausal women. For low-risk women the toxicity outweighs a small gain.

trials.name: monarchE
trials.result: IDFS HR 0.68; 5-y IDFS absolute benefit ≈7.6%; OS benefit reported 2025
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant abemaciclib for high-risk node-positive HR+ disease.

inclusion: HR-positive, HER2-negative, node-positive early breast cancer
Cohort 1: ≥4 nodes, or 1–3 nodes plus grade 3 or tumour ≥5 cm
strengths: Large international trial with OS benefit reported
limitations: Diarrhoea and neutropenia led to dose reductions in many
appraisal.critique: Two years of abemaciclib improves IDFS and now OS in high-risk node-positive disease. Cost and diarrhoea are the main barriers in India.

trials.name: NATALEE
trials.population: HR+, HER2−, stage II–III incl. high-risk N0
trials.takeaway: Ribociclib extends adjuvant CDK4/6 option to a broader stage II–III population.

inclusion: HR-positive, HER2-negative stage II–III early breast cancer
Node-negative allowed if T2 with high grade/Ki-67 or high genomic risk, or T3
strengths: Broader population than monarchE, including high-risk N0
appraisal.critique: Extends adjuvant CDK4/6i to stage II–III disease. Modest absolute benefit, immature OS and cost make case selection important.

trials.name: OlympiA
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant olaparib for high-risk gBRCA carriers; test germline early.

appraisal.critique: One year of olaparib improves IDFS and OS in high-risk gBRCA carriers — a strong reason to test germline BRCA in eligible patients.

trials.name: HERA / NSABP B-31+N9831
trials.result: Recurrence risk reduced ≈50% (joint analysis HR 0.48); OS gain sustained at 10 y
trials.takeaway: One year of adjuvant trastuzumab is standard for HER2+ early BC.

exclusion: Prior cardiac disease or low LVEF
strengths: Large trials with long-term OS benefit
limitations: Crossover in HERA diluted OS difference
Two years no better than one in HERA
appraisal.critique: Trastuzumab transformed HER2+ early breast cancer prognosis. Shorter durations (PERSEPHONE) remain debated, especially where cost is a barrier.

trials.name: APHINITY
trials.result: Small IDFS benefit (HR 0.81), mainly node-positive (6-y absolute 4.5%)
trials.takeaway: Add pertuzumab for node-positive HER2+ disease.

strengths: OS signal emerging in node-positive patients
appraisal.critique: Pertuzumab adds modestly to trastuzumab, mainly in node-positive disease. Its cost-effectiveness for node-negative patients is poor.

trials.name: APT (Tolaney)
trials.takeaway: De-escalated TH is standard for small node-negative HER2+ tumours.

appraisal.critique: Paclitaxel-trastuzumab is now standard for small node-negative HER2+ tumours. Being single-arm, it shows good outcomes but cannot prove equivalence to more intensive therapy.

trials.name: KATHERINE
trials.population: HER2+ with residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy
trials.takeaway: Residual disease after HER2-directed neoadjuvant therapy → T-DM1.

inclusion: Residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane + trastuzumab
strengths: Clear IDFS and now OS benefit
limitations: Most patients did not receive pertuzumab neoadjuvantly
appraisal.critique: Switching to T-DM1 for residual disease cuts recurrence by about half. Its rationale supports giving neoadjuvant therapy to HER2+ tumours ≥T2 or N+.

trials.name: CREATE-X
trials.population: HER2− residual disease after neoadjuvant chemo
trials.result: TNBC subgroup: DFS 69.8% vs 56.1% (HR 0.58), OS HR 0.52
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine for TNBC with residual disease (non-gBRCA or no PARP access).

inclusion: Residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
strengths: Cheap oral drug — very relevant in resource-limited settings
limitations: No anthracycline-taxane standard in all patients
appraisal.critique: Capecitabine improves outcomes for residual TNBC. Data in HR+ disease are weaker, and generalisability beyond East Asian patients was debated but supported by meta-analysis.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-522
arms: Pembrolizumab + carbo-paclitaxel → AC/EC, then adjuvant pembrolizumab
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab + chemo is standard neoadjuvant therapy for stage II–III TNBC.

limitations: Immune-related adverse events, including adrenal insufficiency
Carboplatin added in both arms — differs from many standard regimens
appraisal.critique: Practice-changing for stage II–III TNBC. Questions remain whether all patients need adjuvant pembrolizumab, especially those with pCR.

trials.name: NeoSphere
trials.result: pCR 45.8% with THP vs 29.0% with TH
trials.takeaway: Basis for neoadjuvant dual HER2 blockade (THP).

inclusion: HER2-positive operable, locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer
strengths: Randomised phase 2 showing dual blockade increases pCR
Led to accelerated approval of neoadjuvant pertuzumab
appraisal.critique: Established neoadjuvant pertuzumab-trastuzumab-docetaxel. The pCR advantage is real, but survival benefit relies on APHINITY rather than this trial.

trials.name: CTNeoBC pooled analysis
trials.result: ypT0/is ypN0 strongly associated with EFS (HR 0.48) and OS, most in TNBC and HER2+/HR−
trials.takeaway: pCR is prognostic for individuals; trial-level surrogacy is weak.

inclusion: Neoadjuvant trials with individual patient data (12 trials, ~12,000 patients)
strengths: Showed patient-level association between pCR and survival, especially TNBC and HER2+
limitations: Failed to show trial-level surrogacy — pCR increases did not predict EFS gains
appraisal.critique: pCR is prognostic for individuals but not a validated trial-level surrogate. This is why later trials needed EFS or OS endpoints.

trials.name: CLEOPATRA
trials.result: mPFS 18.7 vs 12.4 mo; mOS 57.1 vs 40.8 mo (HR 0.69)
trials.takeaway: THP is the first-line standard for HER2+ MBC.

inclusion: No prior chemotherapy or anti-HER2 therapy for metastatic disease
exclusion: Relapse within 12 months of adjuvant trastuzumab or chemotherapy
appraisal.critique: A rare trial with an unequivocal large OS benefit. Its population was mostly trastuzumab-naive, unlike most relapsing patients today.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast03
trials.takeaway: T-DXd is the second-line standard for HER2+ MBC.

inclusion: HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer
Progression after trastuzumab and a taxane (advanced or within 6 months of (neo)adjuvant therapy)
Clinically stable, treated brain metastases allowed
exclusion: History of non-infectious ILD/pneumonitis requiring steroids, or current ILD
strengths: Randomised head-to-head superiority over the previous second-line standard
Very large PFS benefit (HR ~0.33) and later OS benefit
Consistent benefit including stable brain metastases
limitations: Drug-related ILD in about 15% (mostly grade 1–2, rare deaths)
Few patients had prior pertuzumab-free first line, so applicability to pertuzumab-naive Indian patients is uncertain
appraisal.critique: T-DXd became the second-line standard for HER2+ MBC. Benefit is unquestioned; the practical issues are ILD surveillance (baseline CT, early steroids) and cost, and its sequencing relative to tucatinib in patients with brain metastases.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast04
trials.population: HER2-low MBC after 1–2 lines of chemo
trials.result: mPFS 9.9 vs 5.1 mo (all); mOS 23.4 vs 16.8 mo (HR 0.64)
trials.takeaway: Created the 'HER2-low' category; T-DXd standard after chemo.

inclusion: 1–2 prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease
limitations: HER2-low IHC scoring is poorly reproducible
appraisal.critique: Practice-changing, but depends on accurate IHC; pathology quality assurance is crucial, especially for borderline 1+ cases.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast06
trials.result: mPFS 13.2 vs 8.1 mo (HR 0.62); similar in HER2-ultralow
trials.takeaway: T-DXd can be used before chemo after endocrine resistance in HER2-low/ultralow.

inclusion: HR-positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer
Progression after ≥2 endocrine lines or within 6 months of CDK4/6i
appraisal.critique: Supports T-DXd before chemotherapy, but some argue sequencing chemotherapy first could preserve T-DXd for later; OS data will decide.

trials.name: HER2CLIMB
trials.population: HER2+ MBC after T, P, T-DM1, incl. brain mets
trials.result: 1-y PFS 33.1% vs 12.3% (HR 0.54); OS HR 0.66; brain-met PFS HR 0.48
trials.takeaway: Tucatinib triplet is preferred with active brain metastases.

inclusion: Brain metastases allowed, including untreated or progressing after local therapy
exclusion: Prior lapatinib (within 12 months) or neratinib, tucatinib or other HER2 TKIs
Brain lesions needing immediate local therapy
strengths: Included patients with active brain metastases — usually excluded from trials
OS benefit overall and in the brain-metastasis subgroup
Oral TKI with good CNS activity
limitations: Diarrhoea, hand-foot syndrome and LFT rise
Benefit after T-DXd not tested in the trial
appraisal.critique: Tucatinib-trastuzumab-capecitabine is the regimen of choice when brain metastases dominate. In the T-DXd era its place is usually third line or for CNS progression.

trials.name: PALOMA-2
trials.population: HR+, HER2− postmenopausal MBC, first line
trials.result: mPFS 24.8 vs 14.5 mo (HR 0.58); OS not significant
trials.takeaway: CDK4/6i + AI established as first-line standard.

inclusion: Postmenopausal HR+, HER2− advanced breast cancer
No prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
exclusion: Prior relapse within 12 months of adjuvant non-steroidal AI
appraisal.critique: Established first-line palbociclib, but unlike ribociclib and abemaciclib it never showed significant OS benefit in this setting.

trials.name: MONALEESA-2
trials.population: HR+, HER2− postmenopausal MBC, first line
trials.result: mPFS 25.3 vs 16.0 mo; mOS 63.9 vs 51.4 mo (HR 0.76)
trials.takeaway: Ribociclib shows OS benefit in first line.

inclusion: Postmenopausal women with HR+, HER2− recurrent or metastatic breast cancer
No prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
Measurable disease or ≥1 lytic bone lesion
exclusion: Relapse during or within 12 months of (neo)adjuvant NSAI
QTcF >450 ms or significant cardiac disease; inflammatory breast cancer; CNS metastases
strengths: Statistically significant OS benefit (~12 months median) with long follow-up
Consistent benefit across subgroups including visceral disease
limitations: Mostly endocrine-sensitive patients — few had relapsed early on adjuvant ET
QTc prolongation, hepatotoxicity and neutropenia require monitoring
appraisal.critique: Ribociclib with letrozole is a preferred first-line option because of proven OS. ECG and LFT monitoring in the first months is mandatory, and drug interactions affecting QTc must be checked.

trials.name: MONALEESA-7
trials.takeaway: First CDK4/6i trial to show OS benefit; standard for premenopausal MBC.

inclusion: Pre- or perimenopausal women, HR+, HER2− advanced breast cancer
No prior endocrine therapy for advanced disease; ≤1 prior chemotherapy line allowed
exclusion: QTc prolongation or significant cardiac disease
strengths: Only phase 3 CDK4/6 trial dedicated to premenopausal women
Allowed one prior line of chemotherapy, reflecting real practice
limitations: Tamoxifen combination raised QTc and is not recommended
Moderate sample size for subgroup analysis
appraisal.critique: Key evidence for OFS + NSAI + ribociclib in young women with metastatic HR+ disease — a large group in India where breast cancer presents younger.

trials.name: MONARCH 3
trials.takeaway: Abemaciclib + AI is a first-line option.

inclusion: Postmenopausal women, HR+, HER2− advanced breast cancer
No prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
exclusion: Relapse within 12 months of adjuvant NSAI
strengths: Benefit also in poor-prognosis groups (liver metastases, short treatment-free interval)
limitations: Final OS benefit numerically ~13 months but not statistically significant
appraisal.critique: Effective first-line partner for AIs. Lack of a significant OS result (unlike MONALEESA-2) has led many guidelines to favour ribociclib, although cross-trial comparison is limited.

trials.name: PADA-1 / SERENA-6
trials.population: HR+ MBC on AI + CDK4/6i with rising ESR1 mutation in ctDNA
trials.takeaway: ctDNA-guided early switch on ESR1 emergence before clinical progression.

inclusion: HR+ HER2− metastatic breast cancer on first-line AI + CDK4/6 inhibitor
Rising ESR1 mutation in serial ctDNA without radiological progression
limitations: PFS gain may partly reflect earlier detection
appraisal.critique: Proof of concept for ctDNA-guided switching. Without OS or quality-of-life gains, whether early switching beats switching at progression remains debated.

trials.name: SOLAR-1
trials.population: HR+, HER2− MBC after AI, PIK3CA-mutant cohort
trials.takeaway: Test PIK3CA; alpelisib + fulvestrant for mutant disease (watch hyperglycaemia).

appraisal.critique: Alpelisib works in PIK3CA-mutant disease but toxicity is significant; capivasertib and inavolisib have since challenged its place.

trials.name: CAPItello-291
trials.population: HR+, HER2− MBC after AI ± CDK4/6i
trials.result: mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo overall (HR 0.60); 7.3 vs 3.1 mo in altered tumours
trials.takeaway: AKT inhibition for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered disease.

inclusion: Relapse or progression on or after AI-based treatment (CDK4/6i allowed, ~70% had it)
≤2 prior endocrine lines and ≤1 chemotherapy line for advanced disease
exclusion: Prior AKT, PI3K or mTOR inhibitor, SERD or fulvestrant
strengths: Dual primary endpoint in overall and AKT-pathway-altered populations
Includes the post-CDK4/6 population seen in practice
limitations: Exploratory data suggest little benefit when PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN are not altered
appraisal.critique: Capivasertib plus fulvestrant is a second-line option for pathway-altered tumours. Testing (tissue or ctDNA) should guide use rather than giving it to all-comers.

trials.name: INAVO120
trials.population: PIK3CA-mut HR+ MBC, endocrine-resistant (relapse ≤12 mo of adjuvant ET)
trials.result: mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo (HR 0.43); OS benefit reported
trials.takeaway: Triplet for PIK3CA-mutant endocrine-resistant first-line disease.

inclusion: PIK3CA-mutated HR+, HER2− advanced breast cancer
Endocrine-resistant: relapse during or within 12 months of adjuvant ET
No prior therapy for advanced disease
appraisal.critique: Establishes a first-line triplet for PIK3CA-mutant endocrine-resistant disease; requires upfront PIK3CA testing.

trials.name: EMERALD
trials.population: HR+ MBC after 1–2 lines ET incl. CDK4/6i
trials.takeaway: First oral SERD approved, for ESR1-mutant disease.

inclusion: ER+, HER2− advanced breast cancer, men and postmenopausal women
1–2 prior endocrine lines including a CDK4/6 inhibitor
exclusion: Prior elacestrant or other investigational SERD
Symptomatic visceral disease or visceral crisis
More than one prior chemotherapy line
strengths: First oral SERD to show benefit in phase 3
limitations: Overall PFS gain small; benefit concentrated in ESR1-mutated tumours
Control arm was endocrine monotherapy (fulvestrant or AI), a weak comparator
appraisal.critique: Elacestrant is reasonable for ESR1-mutated disease after CDK4/6i, especially when endocrine sensitivity was long (≥12 months on prior CDK4/6i). Combination strategies are likely to supersede monotherapy.

trials.name: OlympiAD
trials.takeaway: PARP inhibitor option for gBRCA MBC.

inclusion: Germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
≤2 prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease
Prior anthracycline and taxane; HR+ must have had endocrine therapy
exclusion: Progression on platinum for advanced disease
strengths: Oral targeted therapy with better quality of life than chemotherapy
limitations: No significant OS benefit overall (possible benefit in first line)
appraisal.critique: Olaparib is a tolerable option in gBRCA MBC, but the absence of a platinum comparator means its superiority over carboplatin is unproven.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-355
trials.takeaway: First-line pembrolizumab + chemo for PD-L1 CPS ≥10 metastatic TNBC.

inclusion: Untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC
appraisal.critique: Pembrolizumab with chemotherapy is standard for CPS ≥10 metastatic TNBC; testing PD-L1 with the correct assay is essential.

trials.name: ASCENT
trials.result: mPFS 5.6 vs 1.7 mo; mOS 12.1 vs 6.7 mo (HR 0.48)
trials.takeaway: Sacituzumab is standard later-line therapy for metastatic TNBC.

inclusion: ≥2 prior systemic chemotherapy regimens (one could be adjuvant if relapse within 12 months)
Stable treated brain metastases allowed (excluded from primary analysis)
exclusion: Active or unstable brain metastases (for primary analysis)
strengths: Large PFS and OS benefit (median OS ~12 vs 6.7 months)
Benefit seen across TROP2 expression levels
limitations: Neutropenia and diarrhoea are common; G-CSF often needed
appraisal.critique: Sacituzumab is a standard later-line therapy in TNBC. UGT1A1*28 homozygotes have more toxicity, and supportive care planning is important.

trials.name: TROPiCS-02
trials.population: HR+, HER2− MBC after ET, CDK4/6i and 2–4 chemo lines
trials.result: mPFS 5.5 vs 4.0 mo; mOS 14.4 vs 11.2 mo (HR 0.79)
trials.takeaway: Sacituzumab option for heavily pretreated HR+ MBC.

inclusion: Prior endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitor and taxane
2–4 prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease
strengths: OS benefit in a heavily pretreated population
appraisal.critique: OS gain (~3 months) is modest but real. In HER2-low disease, most clinicians use T-DXd first; sequential ADC benefit appears smaller.

trials.name: NLST
trials.result: Lung cancer mortality reduced 20%; all-cause mortality reduced 6.7%
trials.takeaway: Basis for annual LDCT screening in high-risk smokers.

inclusion: Current smoker or quit within 15 years
exclusion: Symptoms suggesting lung cancer (haemoptysis, weight loss)
strengths: Very large RCT (n=53,454) with lung cancer mortality endpoint
limitations: Chest X-ray comparator rather than no screening
Volunteers healthier and better educated than general smokers
appraisal.critique: First RCT to show screening saves lives (20% relative reduction in lung cancer mortality). False positives, overdiagnosis and an older US population limit direct transfer to India, where TB-related nodules are common.

trials.name: NELSON
trials.result: 10-y lung cancer mortality reduced 24% in men (RR 0.76)
trials.takeaway: Confirmed LDCT benefit with volumetric nodule management and low false-positive rates.

inclusion: Heavy smokers (>15 cigarettes/day for >25 years or >10/day for >30 years)
strengths: Volume-based nodule management cut false positives
appraisal.critique: Confirmed NLST with fewer false positives through volumetric protocols. The structured nodule management is as important as the CT itself.

trials.name: LACE meta-analysis
trials.result: 5-y OS absolute benefit 5.4% (HR 0.89); benefit in stage II–III, not IA
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant cisplatin doublet for resected stage II–IIIA NSCLC.

inclusion: Individual patient data from 5 cisplatin trials (n=4,584)
limitations: No benefit in stage IA, possible harm in IA
Older staging and chemotherapy partners (vinorelbine dominated)
appraisal.critique: Basis for adjuvant cisplatin doublets in stage II–III. The absolute gain is modest, and many patients cannot tolerate cisplatin after lobectomy.

trials.name: ADAURA
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant osimertinib is standard for resected EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

inclusion: Completely resected stage IB–IIIA (7th ed.) non-squamous NSCLC
Adjuvant chemotherapy allowed but not required
strengths: Large DFS benefit and later OS benefit
limitations: Placebo control — no comparison with osimertinib at relapse for all
PET and brain MRI staging not required
appraisal.critique: Osimertinib improved OS, settling much debate, though some argue part of the effect reflects deferral rather than cure. Mandatory EGFR testing in resected non-squamous NSCLC follows.

trials.name: ALINA
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant alectinib replaces chemo for resected ALK+ NSCLC.

inclusion: Completely resected stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA NSCLC (7th ed.)
exclusion: Prior systemic therapy or RT for lung cancer
strengths: Direct comparison with standard adjuvant chemotherapy
Very large DFS benefit (HR ~0.24) including CNS DFS
appraisal.critique: Alectinib replaced adjuvant chemotherapy for resected ALK+ NSCLC. Whether it cures or delays relapse will be answered only by OS.

trials.name: CheckMate 816
trials.result: mEFS 31.6 vs 20.8 mo (HR 0.63); pCR 24.0% vs 2.2%; OS benefit (HR 0.72)
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is standard for resectable NSCLC.

inclusion: Resectable stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA NSCLC (7th ed.)
exclusion: Known EGFR mutation or ALK translocation
strengths: Improved EFS and pCR with only 3 cycles
limitations: No adjuvant phase — optimal total duration unclear
appraisal.critique: Neoadjuvant chemo-IO is standard for resectable NSCLC. Debate continues over neoadjuvant-only vs perioperative approaches.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-671
trials.takeaway: First perioperative IO regimen with OS benefit.

strengths: EFS and OS benefit — first perioperative IO trial with OS
limitations: Cannot separate neoadjuvant from adjuvant contribution
Some patients did not reach surgery
Adjuvant phase adds a year of toxicity and cost
appraisal.critique: Perioperative pembrolizumab is a standard. Whether patients with pCR need adjuvant therapy is unresolved; neoadjuvant-only (CheckMate 816) is an alternative.

trials.name: PACIFIC
trials.population: Unresectable stage III, no progression after concurrent chemoRT
trials.takeaway: Consolidation durvalumab after chemoRT is standard for stage III NSCLC.

inclusion: No progression after ≥2 cycles platinum concurrent chemoRT
limitations: Randomised after chemoRT, so excluded patients who progressed
Post-hoc data suggest little benefit if PD-L1 <1%
appraisal.critique: Durvalumab consolidation is standard after concurrent chemoRT. The selected population (fit, non-progressing) and limited benefit in PD-L1-negative and EGFR-mutant disease are key caveats.

trials.name: LAURA
trials.population: Unresectable stage III EGFR-mutant after chemoRT
trials.takeaway: Consolidation osimertinib (not durvalumab) for EGFR-mutant stage III.

inclusion: No progression after definitive concurrent or sequential platinum chemoRT
strengths: Addresses EGFR-mutant patients who gain little from durvalumab
limitations: Treatment until progression — duration and cost uncertain
appraisal.critique: Osimertinib consolidation is standard for EGFR-mutant stage III. Whether early vs at-progression osimertinib improves OS remains open.

trials.name: RTOG 9410
trials.result: mOS 14.6 vs 17.0 vs 15.6 mo; 5-y OS 10% vs 16% vs 13% (concurrent daily best)
trials.takeaway: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy is superior to sequential.

strengths: Showed concurrent chemoRT improves OS over sequential
limitations: Higher acute oesophagitis with concurrent therapy
BID arm offered no further gain
appraisal.critique: Basis for concurrent chemoRT in fit patients. Sequential remains reasonable for frail or large-volume patients where toxicity is prohibitive.

trials.name: RTOG 0617
trials.result: mOS 28.7 mo (60 Gy) vs 20.3 mo (74 Gy); cetuximab no benefit; heart dose predicted death
trials.takeaway: 60 Gy remains standard; dose escalation is harmful; limit heart dose.

strengths: Definitive evidence that 74 Gy is harmful
Factorial design also showed cetuximab adds nothing
limitations: Survival deficit with high dose not fully explained
Variation in centre experience and RT technique (3D vs IMRT)
appraisal.critique: 60 Gy remains standard. The trial made heart and lung dose constraints central to thoracic RT planning.

trials.name: CHART
trials.takeaway: Shows accelerated fractionation benefit (repopulation); informs hypofractionation when concurrent not feasible.

strengths: Survival benefit (~9% at 2 years) from accelerated treatment
limitations: Three fractions daily over 12 consecutive days — logistically demanding
appraisal.critique: Showed overall treatment time matters, but logistics prevented adoption. Concurrent chemoRT superseded it.

trials.name: Lung ART
trials.result: 3-y DFS 47.1% vs 43.8% (NS); more cardiopulmonary deaths with PORT
trials.takeaway: Routine PORT is not recommended for completely resected pN2.

strengths: Randomised data on PORT in pN2
limitations: Mediastinal relapse halved but no DFS gain
appraisal.critique: Routine PORT is not recommended in pN2. Selected patients (extracapsular extension, multiple stations) may still benefit.

trials.name: CHISEL
trials.result: Local failure HR 0.32; longer OS with SABR
trials.takeaway: SABR is standard for medically inoperable stage I NSCLC.

strengths: Randomised evidence for SABR over conventional RT
appraisal.critique: Supports SABR as standard for inoperable early NSCLC, although the sample is small.

trials.name: SABR-COMET
trials.result: mOS 50 vs 28 mo; 5-y OS 42.3% vs 17.7%; grade 5 toxicity 4.5%
trials.takeaway: Supports ablative RT to all sites in oligometastatic disease; phase 3 confirmation ongoing.

limitations: Imbalance favouring prostate primaries in SABR arm
appraisal.critique: Hypothesis-generating rather than definitive. Phase 3 trials (SABR-COMET-3, -10) are needed before widespread use.

trials.name: Gomez (MDACC) oligomet NSCLC
trials.result: mPFS 14.2 vs 4.4 mo; mOS 41.2 vs 17.0 mo
trials.takeaway: Consolidative local therapy for oligometastatic NSCLC after systemic response.

inclusion: No progression after first-line systemic therapy
appraisal.critique: Strong signal for consolidative local therapy in oligometastatic NSCLC. Its relevance in the immunotherapy era is being tested.

trials.name: IPASS
trials.population: East Asian never/light smokers with adenocarcinoma
trials.result: EGFR-mutant: PFS HR 0.48; EGFR wild-type: HR 2.85 (worse with gefitinib)
trials.takeaway: EGFR mutation, not clinical features, predicts TKI benefit; established biomarker-driven therapy.

inclusion: East Asian patients with stage IIIB/IV adenocarcinoma
strengths: Showed EGFR mutation as predictive biomarker
limitations: OS not different because of crossover
appraisal.critique: Gefitinib was better only in EGFR-mutant tumours and worse in wild-type, making EGFR testing mandatory before first-line therapy.

trials.name: FLAURA
trials.result: mPFS 18.9 vs 10.2 mo; mOS 38.6 vs 31.8 mo (HR 0.80)
trials.takeaway: Osimertinib is first-line standard for EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

inclusion: Advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R
strengths: PFS (18.9 vs 10.2 months) and OS benefit
limitations: OS benefit not seen in Asian subgroup
Comparator first-generation TKIs; many control patients never received osimertinib
appraisal.critique: Osimertinib became first-line standard. The Asian subgroup result and comparator choice are the main criticisms.

trials.name: FLAURA2
trials.takeaway: Adding chemo to osimertinib prolongs survival, notably with brain mets or high burden.

strengths: Greater benefit in CNS metastases and L858R
limitations: More chemotherapy toxicity and time in clinic
appraisal.critique: Adding chemotherapy to osimertinib helps, but at a toxicity cost. It is best for higher-risk patients (CNS metastases, L858R, TP53 co-mutation, high ctDNA).

trials.name: MARIPOSA
trials.takeaway: Amivantamab-lazertinib is a first-line alternative; more toxicity (VTE prophylaxis, skin).

strengths: PFS and OS benefit over osimertinib
limitations: IV amivantamab with infusion reactions, rash, paronychia and VTE
appraisal.critique: Effective combination, but toxicity and logistics limit uptake, especially in resource-limited settings. A subcutaneous formulation may help.

trials.name: ALEX
trials.result: mPFS 34.8 vs 10.9 mo; CNS progression 12% vs 45%
trials.takeaway: Alectinib is a first-line standard for ALK+ NSCLC.

limitations: Comparator crizotinib has weak CNS penetration
appraisal.critique: Alectinib became first-line standard for ALK+ NSCLC.

trials.name: CROWN
trials.result: 5-y PFS 60% vs 8% (HR 0.19); intracranial progression strongly reduced
trials.takeaway: Lorlatinib offers the longest PFS in ALK+ disease; manage lipids and CNS effects.

limitations: Neurocognitive and mood effects, weight gain, hyperlipidaemia
appraisal.critique: Lorlatinib offers the longest PFS; neurocognitive toxicity and lipid monitoring are key.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-024
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab monotherapy for PD-L1 ≥50% NSCLC.

limitations: Chemotherapy comparator without pemetrexed maintenance in all
appraisal.critique: Pembrolizumab monotherapy is standard for PD-L1 ≥50%. Many patients still progress early; chemo-IO is an alternative in high-burden disease.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-189
trials.takeaway: Chemo-IO standard for non-squamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1.

appraisal.critique: Chemo-pembrolizumab is the standard for non-squamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-407
trials.takeaway: Chemo-IO standard for squamous NSCLC.

appraisal.critique: Chemo-pembrolizumab is standard for squamous NSCLC.

trials.name: CheckMate 9LA
trials.takeaway: Dual IO + limited chemo is a first-line option.

strengths: OS benefit, especially in squamous and PD-L1 <1%
appraisal.critique: An option for PD-L1-negative or squamous disease; toxicity is a trade-off.

trials.name: PARAMOUNT
trials.takeaway: Continuation pemetrexed maintenance improves survival.

inclusion: No progression after 4 cycles of cisplatin-pemetrexed
appraisal.critique: Established pemetrexed maintenance, now incorporated into chemo-IO regimens.

trials.name: Scagliotti cis-pem vs cis-gem
trials.result: OS equal overall; adenocarcinoma 12.6 vs 10.9 mo, squamous worse with pemetrexed
trials.takeaway: Histology guides chemo: pemetrexed for non-squamous only.

strengths: Revealed histology as a predictive factor
limitations: Non-inferiority design; histology finding was a pre-planned subgroup
appraisal.critique: Made histology essential for chemotherapy choice — pemetrexed for non-squamous, gemcitabine for squamous.

trials.name: Temel early palliative care
trials.result: Better QoL, less depression, less aggressive end-of-life care; mOS 11.6 vs 8.9 mo
trials.takeaway: Integrate palliative care early in metastatic disease.

strengths: Improved quality of life and mood
Longer survival despite less aggressive end-of-life care
appraisal.critique: Strong case for early integrated palliative care; generalisability to resource-limited settings needs local models.

trials.name: CodeBreaK 200
trials.population: KRAS G12C NSCLC after platinum and IO
trials.result: mPFS 5.6 vs 4.5 mo (HR 0.66); no OS difference
trials.takeaway: KRAS G12C inhibitor is a second-line option.

inclusion: Progression after platinum chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibitor
exclusion: Prior KRAS G12C inhibitor or docetaxel
strengths: First randomised phase 3 of a KRAS G12C inhibitor
limitations: Modest PFS gain (5.6 vs 4.5 months), no OS benefit
Crossover and early dropouts in docetaxel arm
FDA raised concerns about assessment bias
appraisal.critique: Sotorasib is modestly better than docetaxel. The modest gain and bias concerns led to scepticism and a withheld full approval.

trials.name: LIBRETTO-431
trials.takeaway: Selpercatinib first line for RET-fusion NSCLC.

exclusion: Prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
appraisal.critique: Supports first-line selpercatinib and broad NGS panels at diagnosis.

trials.name: DESTINY-Lung01/02
trials.result: ORR 49% at 5.4 mg/kg; ILD ~13% (lower than 6.4 mg/kg)
trials.takeaway: T-DXd for pretreated HER2-mutant NSCLC.

appraisal.critique: Led to accelerated approval; randomised data are pending.

trials.name: CONVERT
trials.result: mOS 30 vs 25 mo (NS); 2-y OS 56% vs 51%; similar toxicity
trials.takeaway: 45 Gy BID remains standard; 66 Gy daily is an alternative.

limitations: Designed for superiority of once daily — failed
appraisal.critique: Twice-daily 45 Gy remains standard, but 66 Gy once daily is acceptable when BID is impractical.

trials.name: Turrisi INT 0096
trials.takeaway: Twice-daily concurrent thoracic RT established.

strengths: Showed accelerated BID RT improves survival
limitations: Once-daily arm only 45 Gy — low dose
appraisal.critique: Basis for 45 Gy BID. The low once-daily dose made the comparison unfair, prompting CONVERT and CALGB 30610.

trials.name: Aupérin PCI meta-analysis
trials.result: 3-y OS 20.7% vs 15.3%; brain mets reduced by 54%
trials.takeaway: PCI after CR in limited-stage SCLC (MRI surveillance increasingly used).

limitations: Mostly limited-stage; brain imaging not mandatory
appraisal.critique: PCI benefits patients with complete response, but with MRI surveillance the case for PCI is being re-examined.

trials.name: ADRIATIC
trials.population: LS-SCLC without progression after concurrent chemoRT
trials.takeaway: Consolidation durvalumab is standard after chemoRT in LS-SCLC.

inclusion: No progression after concurrent platinum-etoposide chemoRT
strengths: OS and PFS benefit — first major LS-SCLC advance in decades
appraisal.critique: Durvalumab consolidation is a new standard in LS-SCLC.

trials.name: IMpower133
trials.takeaway: Chemo-IO is first-line standard for ES-SCLC.

appraisal.critique: Small but real OS benefit; a minority are long-term survivors.

trials.name: CASPIAN
trials.takeaway: Durvalumab + EP is an alternative first-line chemo-IO.

inclusion: Asymptomatic or treated brain metastases allowed
strengths: Allowed cisplatin or carboplatin and up to 4 cycles
limitations: PCI not allowed in IO arm
appraisal.critique: Confirms chemo-IO as first-line standard in ES-SCLC.

trials.name: CREST (Slotman)
trials.takeaway: Consolidative thoracic RT considered for residual thoracic disease after chemo.

inclusion: ES-SCLC with response to 4–6 cycles chemotherapy
appraisal.critique: Supports consolidative thoracic RT in responders with residual thoracic disease; its role with IO is under study.

trials.name: DeLLphi-304
trials.takeaway: Tarlatamab is the second-line standard for SCLC.

inclusion: SCLC progressing after first-line platinum chemotherapy (± immunotherapy)
limitations: Requires inpatient monitoring for first doses
appraisal.critique: Tarlatamab is a new second-line standard; logistics of CRS monitoring matter.

trials.name: CROSS
trials.result: mOS 49.4 vs 24.0 mo; pCR 29% (49% in SCC)
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CROSS) is standard, especially for SCC.

inclusion: Resectable oesophageal or GEJ carcinoma (SCC or adenocarcinoma)
strengths: Low-toxicity regimen with high pCR (49% in SCC)
limitations: Larger benefit in SCC than adenocarcinoma
appraisal.critique: Standard neoadjuvant chemoRT, especially for SCC. For adenocarcinoma, ESOPEC has challenged it in favour of FLOT.

trials.name: CheckMate 577
trials.population: Oesophageal/GEJ cancer with residual disease after CROSS + surgery
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab for residual pathologic disease after neoadjuvant chemoRT.

inclusion: Residual pathological disease after neoadjuvant chemoRT and R0 resection
strengths: Doubled DFS in a high-risk group
limitations: Does not address patients receiving FLOT
appraisal.critique: Adjuvant nivolumab is standard after CROSS with residual disease, though the absence of OS benefit tempers enthusiasm.

trials.name: FLOT4
trials.takeaway: Perioperative FLOT is standard for resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma.

inclusion: Resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2+ and/or cN+
strengths: OS benefit over ECF/ECX (median 50 vs 35 months)
limitations: Mostly European population with GEJ predominance
appraisal.critique: FLOT is the perioperative standard for fit patients. Many cannot complete the postoperative phase; adding immunotherapy (MATTERHORN) is the next step.

trials.name: ESOPEC
trials.takeaway: FLOT preferred over CROSS for oesophageal adenocarcinoma.

inclusion: Resectable oesophageal adenocarcinoma cT1N+ or cT2–4a any N
Fit for surgery and both regimens
limitations: Open-label; CROSS arm had low adjuvant therapy use
Not all CROSS patients received nivolumab
appraisal.critique: Favours perioperative FLOT for oesophageal adenocarcinoma. Critics note the CROSS arm lacked adjuvant nivolumab now standard.

trials.name: MAGIC
trials.takeaway: Established perioperative chemotherapy in gastric cancer.

inclusion: Resectable gastric, GEJ or lower oesophageal adenocarcinoma
strengths: First to show OS benefit for perioperative chemotherapy (5-year OS 36% vs 23%)
appraisal.critique: Established perioperative chemotherapy; FLOT has since superseded ECF.

trials.name: INT-0116 (Macdonald)
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant chemoRT benefit, mainly after limited (D0/D1) dissection.

inclusion: Resected gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, stage IB–IV (M0)
limitations: Only ~10% had D2 dissection — chemoRT compensated for inadequate surgery
appraisal.critique: Benefit largely reflects inadequate surgery. After D2 gastrectomy, adjuvant chemotherapy (CLASSIC) is preferred; ARTIST trials showed limited added value of RT.

trials.name: CLASSIC
trials.population: Stage II–IIIB gastric cancer after D2 gastrectomy
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant CAPOX after D2 gastrectomy (Asian standard).

strengths: DFS and OS benefit for adjuvant CAPOX after D2 surgery
appraisal.critique: Adjuvant CAPOX is standard after upfront D2 gastrectomy, which is common practice in India for operable gastric cancer.

trials.name: ToGA
trials.result: mOS 13.8 vs 11.1 mo; 16.0 vs 11.8 mo in IHC3+ / IHC2+FISH+
trials.takeaway: Test HER2 in all advanced gastric cancer; add trastuzumab.

inclusion: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or FISH+) advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma
strengths: Defined HER2 testing criteria in gastric cancer
limitations: Benefit mainly in IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/FISH+
Heterogeneous HER2 expression in gastric tumours
appraisal.critique: Trastuzumab with chemotherapy is standard for HER2+ gastric cancer; correct HER2 scoring (gastric-specific criteria) is critical.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-811
trials.result: ORR 74% vs 52%; benefit confined to PD-L1 CPS ≥1 (OS HR 0.79)
trials.takeaway: Add pembrolizumab for HER2+ CPS ≥1 disease.

limitations: Initial approval based on ORR alone
appraisal.critique: Adds pembrolizumab for PD-L1-positive HER2+ disease.

trials.name: CheckMate 649
trials.takeaway: Chemo-nivolumab first line, greatest benefit with higher CPS.

inclusion: HER2-negative advanced gastric, GEJ or oesophageal adenocarcinoma
strengths: Large global trial including Asian patients
limitations: Little or no benefit in CPS <1
appraisal.critique: Nivolumab plus chemotherapy is standard, ideally for higher PD-L1 expressers.

trials.name: SPOTLIGHT / GLOW
trials.takeaway: Test CLDN18.2; zolbetuximab is a first-line option (nausea/vomiting common).

inclusion: Claudin 18.2-positive (≥75% tumour cells moderate-strong staining), HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma
exclusion: Gastric outlet obstruction or complete dysphagia
strengths: OS benefit in a new biomarker-selected population
limitations: Nausea and vomiting are frequent, especially with first dose
appraisal.critique: Zolbetuximab adds a targeted option; sequencing with IO remains unclear.

trials.name: RAINBOW
trials.takeaway: Paclitaxel-ramucirumab is the second-line standard.

inclusion: Progression within 4 months of first-line platinum + fluoropyrimidine
appraisal.critique: Ramucirumab-paclitaxel remains a second-line standard.

trials.name: CheckMate 648 / KEYNOTE-590
trials.population: Advanced oesophageal SCC (± adenocarcinoma in KN-590)
trials.takeaway: Chemo-IO first line for oesophageal SCC, best with PD-L1 positivity.

inclusion: Advanced or metastatic oesophageal SCC (KN-590 also adenocarcinoma/Siewert I GEJ)
exclusion: Prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
limitations: Benefit driven by PD-L1-positive tumours (CPS ≥10 / TPS ≥1%)
appraisal.critique: Chemo-IO is first-line standard for oesophageal SCC, particularly with PD-L1 expression.

trials.name: RTOG 85-01
trials.takeaway: Definitive chemoRT (50–50.4 Gy) is standard non-surgical therapy.

strengths: Showed chemoRT superior to RT alone, with long-term survivors (~26% at 5 years)
appraisal.critique: Basis for definitive chemoRT in oesophageal cancer.

trials.name: INT 0123
trials.result: No benefit from 64.8 Gy; more treatment deaths
trials.takeaway: 50.4 Gy remains the standard definitive dose.

strengths: Showed no benefit for dose escalation
limitations: Most deaths in high-dose arm occurred before 50.4 Gy
appraisal.critique: 50.4 Gy remains standard. The high-dose arm's excess deaths occurred at low dose, so the trial's conclusion is often debated.

trials.name: MOSAIC
trials.takeaway: Oxaliplatin-based adjuvant therapy is standard for stage III colon cancer.

strengths: DFS and OS benefit for stage III
limitations: No OS benefit in stage II
appraisal.critique: FOLFOX is standard for stage III; stage II benefit is minimal and limited to high-risk features.

trials.name: IDEA
trials.result: Low-risk (T1–3 N1): 3 mo CAPOX non-inferior; less neuropathy
trials.takeaway: 3 months CAPOX for low-risk stage III; 6 months for high-risk (T4 or N2).

inclusion: Stage III colon cancer after resection
strengths: Large pooled analysis guiding risk-based duration
appraisal.critique: 3 months CAPOX for low-risk stage III is standard, reducing neuropathy; FOLFOX for 6 months for high-risk disease.

trials.name: ATOMIC
trials.population: Resected stage III dMMR colon cancer
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant atezolizumab + FOLFOX for stage III dMMR colon cancer.

inclusion: Resected stage III dMMR colon cancer
appraisal.critique: Adding atezolizumab to FOLFOX is a new standard for stage III dMMR colon cancer.

trials.name: NICHE-2
trials.result: Major pathologic response 95%, pCR 68%; no recurrences at 2 y
trials.takeaway: Short neoadjuvant IO is highly active in dMMR colon cancer.

inclusion: Locally advanced (cT3 and/or N+) dMMR colon cancer
strengths: Very high pCR rate (~68%) with short IO
appraisal.critique: Strong signal for neoadjuvant IO in dMMR colon cancer; randomised data are needed.

trials.name: Cercek dostarlimab dMMR rectal
trials.result: cCR 100% in first 12, sustained in expanded cohort; organ preservation without RT or surgery
trials.takeaway: Anti-PD-1 alone can replace chemoRT and surgery in dMMR rectal cancer.

strengths: 100% clinical complete response in early cohort
Organ preservation without surgery or RT
appraisal.critique: Paradigm-shifting for dMMR rectal cancer; small numbers mean careful follow-up remains essential.

trials.name: German CAO/ARO/AIO-94
trials.result: Local recurrence 6% vs 13% (5-y); no OS difference; less toxicity preop
trials.takeaway: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy is preferred over postoperative.

strengths: Lower local recurrence and toxicity with preoperative chemoRT
appraisal.critique: Preoperative chemoRT became standard.

trials.name: Dutch TME
trials.takeaway: Short-course RT reduces local recurrence even with optimal TME surgery.

strengths: Standardised TME surgery with quality control
appraisal.critique: Short-course RT reduces local recurrence even with good TME surgery.

trials.name: RAPIDO
trials.result: 3-y DrTF 23.7% vs 30.4% (HR 0.75); pCR 28% vs 14%; later higher locoregional failure
trials.takeaway: Total neoadjuvant therapy with short-course RT is a standard option.

inclusion: High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer (cT4, N2, EMVI+, MRF+, lateral nodes)
limitations: Higher locoregional recurrence in long-term follow-up
appraisal.critique: Supports total neoadjuvant therapy, but concerns about local recurrence remain.

trials.name: PRODIGE 23
trials.result: 3-y DFS 76% vs 69% (HR 0.69); pCR 28% vs 12%; OS benefit at 7 y
trials.takeaway: Induction FOLFIRINOX TNT improves outcomes in rectal cancer.

appraisal.critique: Total neoadjuvant therapy with FOLFIRINOX improves outcomes for fit patients.

trials.name: OPRA
trials.takeaway: Consolidation-chemo TNT enables watch-and-wait organ preservation for ~half.

strengths: Organ preservation in ~half with consolidation chemotherapy
appraisal.critique: Watch-and-wait is feasible with consolidation TNT; long-term data needed.

trials.name: PROSPECT
trials.population: cT2N+ / cT3N0–1 rectal cancer suitable for sphincter-sparing surgery
arms: Neoadjuvant FOLFOX (chemoRT only if poor response)
trials.takeaway: Selective omission of pelvic RT in intermediate-risk rectal cancer.

strengths: Showed FOLFOX alone is non-inferior to chemoRT
appraisal.critique: Pelvic RT can be omitted in selected intermediate-risk rectal cancer.

trials.name: CRYSTAL
trials.takeaway: Anti-EGFR benefit restricted to RAS wild-type tumours.

exclusion: Prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease
appraisal.critique: Established anti-EGFR therapy in RAS wild-type mCRC.

trials.name: FIRE-3 / CALGB 80405
trials.result: Left-sided primaries: OS favoured anti-EGFR; right-sided favoured bevacizumab
trials.takeaway: Primary tumour sidedness guides biologic choice in RAS wild-type mCRC.

exclusion: Prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease
appraisal.critique: Anti-EGFR preferred for left-sided RAS wild-type tumours.

trials.name: PARADIGM
trials.takeaway: Prospectively confirmed anti-EGFR for left-sided RAS wild-type mCRC.

appraisal.critique: Panitumumab-FOLFOX is standard for left-sided RAS/BRAF wild-type mCRC.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-177
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab is first-line standard for MSI-H mCRC.

exclusion: Prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease
limitations: OS not statistically significant due to crossover
appraisal.critique: Pembrolizumab is first-line standard for MSI-H mCRC; early progressors need attention.

trials.name: CheckMate 8HW
trials.result: vs chemo: 2-y PFS 72% vs 14% (HR 0.21); better than nivolumab alone
trials.takeaway: Nivolumab + ipilimumab is a first-line option for MSI-H mCRC.

appraisal.critique: Nivolumab-ipilimumab is an option; toxicity balance needed.

trials.name: BEACON CRC / BREAKWATER
trials.result: BEACON mOS 9.3 vs 5.9 mo; BREAKWATER 1L ORR 61% vs 40%, OS benefit
trials.takeaway: Test BRAF; encorafenib + cetuximab (+ chemo first line) for BRAF V600E.

inclusion: BEACON: after 1–2 lines; BREAKWATER: first line
strengths: OS benefit in a poor-prognosis group
limitations: Triplet arm not superior in BEACON
appraisal.critique: Encorafenib-cetuximab is standard; first-line combination with FOLFOX is now emerging.

trials.name: DESTINY-CRC / MOUNTAINEER
trials.result: MOUNTAINEER ORR 38%; DESTINY-CRC02 ORR ~38% at 5.4 mg/kg
trials.takeaway: HER2-targeted options for HER2-amplified mCRC.

appraisal.critique: Supports HER2 testing in mCRC; randomised data are limited.

trials.name: CORRECT / RECOURSE / SUNLIGHT
trials.result: SUNLIGHT: mOS 10.8 vs 7.5 mo (HR 0.61) adding bevacizumab
trials.takeaway: Trifluridine-tipiracil + bevacizumab is preferred third-line.

inclusion: Prior fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, anti-VEGF ± anti-EGFR
strengths: SUNLIGHT showed added benefit with bevacizumab
appraisal.critique: FTD-TPI + bevacizumab is preferred; regorafenib remains an option.

trials.name: FRESCO-2
trials.takeaway: Fruquintinib is a later-line option.

inclusion: Refractory metastatic CRC after standard therapies including FTD-TPI or regorafenib
strengths: OS benefit in heavily pretreated patients
appraisal.critique: Fruquintinib is an additional late-line option.

trials.name: EORTC 40983 (EPOC)
trials.result: 3-y PFS improved 7–9% absolute; no OS difference
trials.takeaway: Perioperative chemo is an option around liver metastasectomy.

appraisal.critique: Perioperative FOLFOX is reasonable; OS benefit unproven.

trials.name: ACT II
trials.result: No benefit from cisplatin or maintenance; ~90% complete response
trials.takeaway: 5-FU/mitomycin with RT remains the standard (Nigro regimen).

appraisal.critique: 5-FU/mitomycin with RT remains standard.

trials.name: RTOG 98-11
trials.result: 5-y DFS 67.8% vs 57.8%; colostomy higher with cisplatin
trials.takeaway: Confirms mitomycin-based chemoRT without induction chemotherapy.

appraisal.critique: Confirmed mitomycin-based chemoRT as standard.

trials.name: POD1UM-303
trials.takeaway: First chemo-IO standard for advanced anal SCC.

appraisal.critique: First positive IO trial in anal cancer; adds retifanlimab to first-line chemotherapy.

trials.name: CONKO-001
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant chemo is standard after pancreatic resection.

inclusion: Macroscopically complete (R0/R1) resection of pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Postoperative CA19-9 <2.5× upper limit of normal
exclusion: Distant metastases or macroscopic residual disease
strengths: First trial to show adjuvant gemcitabine improves DFS and OS
limitations: Excluded patients with high post-op CA19-9, a poor-prognosis group
appraisal.critique: Established adjuvant chemotherapy after pancreatic resection. Gemcitabine alone is now reserved for patients unfit for mFOLFIRINOX or gem-cap.

trials.name: ESPAC-4
trials.takeaway: Gem-cape is the adjuvant option for patients unfit for mFOLFIRINOX.

inclusion: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (R0 or R1)
limitations: OS advantage driven partly by R0 patients
appraisal.critique: Gem-cap is the adjuvant regimen for patients not fit for mFOLFIRINOX. With PRODIGE 24 it shows combination therapy beats gemcitabine alone.

trials.name: PRODIGE 24
trials.result: mOS 53.5 vs 35.5 mo; mDFS 21.4 vs 12.8 mo
trials.takeaway: mFOLFIRINOX is the adjuvant standard for fit patients.

limitations: Many in India are not fit enough post-Whipple
appraisal.critique: mFOLFIRINOX is the adjuvant standard for fit patients; dose modifications are common, and patient selection is key.

trials.name: ACCORD 11 (PRODIGE 4)
trials.takeaway: FOLFIRINOX first line for fit patients.

strengths: First regimen to beat gemcitabine by a wide margin
appraisal.critique: FOLFIRINOX is standard for fit patients with metastatic disease. Modified doses are used widely to improve tolerability.

trials.name: MPACT
trials.takeaway: Gem-nab-paclitaxel is a first-line standard.

inclusion: No prior treatment for metastatic disease
appraisal.critique: Gem-nab-paclitaxel is standard for patients who cannot tolerate FOLFIRINOX. No head-to-head comparison with FOLFIRINOX exists.

trials.name: NAPOLI-3
trials.takeaway: NALIRIFOX is an approved first-line option.

strengths: OS benefit over gem-nab-paclitaxel (11.1 vs 9.2 months)
appraisal.critique: NALIRIFOX is an option, but many view it as FOLFIRINOX with a costlier irinotecan; FOLFIRINOX remains equally reasonable.

trials.name: POLO
trials.population: gBRCA metastatic pancreatic cancer stable after ≥16 weeks platinum
trials.result: mPFS 7.4 vs 3.8 mo (HR 0.53); no OS difference
trials.takeaway: Germline testing for all; olaparib maintenance for gBRCA.

inclusion: No progression after ≥16 weeks of first-line platinum
limitations: Placebo comparator; continuing platinum not tested
appraisal.critique: Olaparib maintenance gives a chemotherapy break but no proven survival gain; continuing platinum is a reasonable alternative. Germline testing for all pancreatic cancers is supported.

trials.name: RASolute 302
trials.takeaway: First RAS(ON) inhibitor to improve survival; approved 2026.

inclusion: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma progressing after one prior line of therapy
strengths: OS benefit (~13 vs 7 months) for a RAS(ON) inhibitor
limitations: Recent data — long-term toxicity and durability still emerging
appraisal.critique: Daraxonrasib appears to be a major advance in second-line PDAC; real-world availability and cost in India are yet to be defined.

trials.name: PREOPANC
trials.takeaway: Supports neoadjuvant therapy, especially for borderline resectable disease.

inclusion: Resectable or borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma
strengths: Long-term OS benefit for neoadjuvant chemoRT
limitations: Gemcitabine-based regimen — not modern multi-agent chemotherapy
Primary OS endpoint not significant initially; benefit emerged with longer follow-up
appraisal.critique: Supports a neoadjuvant approach, especially for borderline resectable disease. PREOPANC-2 and others test FOLFIRINOX-based strategies.

trials.name: SHARP
trials.takeaway: First systemic therapy to prolong survival in HCC.

inclusion: Advanced HCC not amenable to surgery or locoregional therapy
strengths: First systemic therapy to improve OS in HCC (10.7 vs 7.9 months)
appraisal.critique: Established systemic therapy for HCC; now superseded by IO combinations but still used where IO is unaffordable.

trials.name: REFLECT
trials.takeaway: Lenvatinib is a TKI first-line option.

strengths: Non-inferior OS to sorafenib with better PFS and response
limitations: Excluded high-risk patients (main portal vein invasion)
appraisal.critique: Lenvatinib is an alternative first-line option when immunotherapy is not suitable.

trials.name: IMbrave150
trials.takeaway: Atezo-bev is first-line standard; screen varices before bevacizumab.

exclusion: Untreated or incompletely treated varices with bleeding risk
Main portal vein thrombosis with high risk (some)
limitations: Bleeding risk requiring endoscopy before treatment
appraisal.critique: Atezolizumab-bevacizumab is the first-line standard. Upper GI endoscopy and variceal management must precede treatment.

trials.name: HIMALAYA
trials.takeaway: STRIDE is a first-line option, especially with bleeding risk.

strengths: Durable OS benefit with long follow-up
limitations: Single priming dose of tremelimumab may be impractical in some settings
appraisal.critique: STRIDE is an option for patients with bleeding risk or contraindications to bevacizumab.

trials.name: CheckMate 9DW
trials.takeaway: Dual checkpoint blockade is another first-line option.

strengths: OS benefit over lenvatinib or sorafenib
appraisal.critique: Nivo-ipi is another first-line option; choice among IO regimens depends on comorbidities and access.

trials.name: TOPAZ-1
trials.takeaway: Gem-cis + durvalumab (or pembrolizumab, KEYNOTE-966) is first-line standard.

inclusion: Advanced biliary tract cancer (intrahepatic, extrahepatic, gallbladder)
appraisal.critique: Durvalumab-gem-cis is first-line standard; relevant to India where gallbladder cancer is common.

trials.name: ABC-02
trials.takeaway: Gem-cis became the backbone for biliary cancer.

appraisal.critique: Established gem-cis as standard backbone for advanced biliary cancer.

trials.name: BILCAP
trials.result: Per-protocol mOS 53 vs 36 mo (HR 0.75); ITT not significant
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine is standard after biliary resection.

appraisal.critique: Capecitabine is standard adjuvant therapy, though the evidence is modest.

trials.name: ClarIDHy / FIGHT-202
trials.takeaway: Molecular profiling (IDH1, FGFR2, HER2, BRAF, MSI) is essential in cholangiocarcinoma.

exclusion: Prior targeted therapy against same target
strengths: Established targeted therapy in biliary cancer
limitations: Modest PFS in ClarIDHy; OS benefit only after crossover adjustment
appraisal.critique: Supports molecular testing in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

trials.name: NETTER-1
trials.population: SSTR+ midgut NET progressing on octreotide
trials.result: 20-mo PFS 65.2% vs 10.8%; final OS 48.0 vs 36.3 mo (NS)
trials.takeaway: PRRT is standard second-line for SSTR+ midgut NET.

appraisal.critique: PRRT is the standard second-line therapy for midgut NET.

trials.name: NETTER-2
trials.takeaway: First-line PRRT for higher-grade well-differentiated GEP-NET.

appraisal.critique: First-line PRRT is an option for higher-grade NETs.

trials.name: PROMID / CLARINET
trials.takeaway: Somatostatin analogues have antiproliferative effect.

inclusion: Well-differentiated GEP-NET (midgut in PROMID; GEP-NET with Ki-67 <10% in CLARINET)
appraisal.critique: SSAs are first-line therapy for well-differentiated NETs.

trials.name: RADIANT-3/4 & SUN-1111
trials.population: Advanced pancreatic NET (RADIANT-3, SUN) / lung-GI NET (RADIANT-4)
trials.result: RADIANT-3 mPFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo; sunitinib 11.4 vs 5.5 mo
trials.takeaway: Everolimus and sunitinib are standard for progressive pNET.

inclusion: Advanced pancreatic (RADIANT-3, SUN) or lung/GI NET (RADIANT-4)
appraisal.critique: Everolimus and sunitinib are options after SSAs.

trials.name: E2211 (CAPTEM)
trials.takeaway: CAPTEM is an active cytotoxic option for pNET.

appraisal.critique: CAPTEM is an effective option for pancreatic NETs.

trials.name: PIVOT / ProtecT
trials.result: 15-y PCa mortality ~3% in all arms; metastasis higher with monitoring
trials.takeaway: Active surveillance is safe for low-risk disease; treatment reduces progression, not death.

limitations: Mostly low-risk disease; monitoring less rigorous than modern active surveillance (no MRI)
appraisal.critique: No prostate cancer mortality difference at 15 years, but more progression and metastasis with monitoring. Each treatment has a distinct toxicity profile, making shared decisions essential.

trials.name: RTOG 94-08
trials.result: 10-y OS 62% vs 57%; benefit in intermediate risk
trials.takeaway: Short-term ADT with RT for intermediate-risk disease.

strengths: OS benefit for short-term ADT with RT (10-year OS 62% vs 57%)
limitations: RT dose 66.6 Gy — below modern dose-escalated standards
appraisal.critique: Short-course ADT benefits intermediate-risk disease; with modern dose escalation its magnitude is debated, and favourable intermediate risk may skip it.

trials.name: Bolla EORTC 22863
trials.takeaway: Long-term ADT (2–3 y) with RT is standard for high-risk disease.

inclusion: Locally advanced (T3–4) or high-grade T1–2 prostate cancer
strengths: OS benefit for long-term ADT with RT
appraisal.critique: Established long-term ADT with RT for high-risk disease; duration (18–36 months) remains individualised.

trials.name: CHHiP
trials.result: 5-y freedom from failure 88.3% (74 Gy) vs 90.6% (60 Gy) vs 85.9% (57 Gy)
trials.takeaway: 60 Gy/20 fr moderate hypofractionation is a standard.

appraisal.critique: 60 Gy/20 is standard moderate hypofractionation and saves 3 weeks of treatment.

trials.name: HYPO-RT-PC / PACE-B
trials.takeaway: 5-fraction SBRT is a standard option for low/intermediate-risk disease.

limitations: Higher acute GU toxicity in HYPO-RT-PC
appraisal.critique: Ultra-hypofractionation (5 fractions) is a standard option for low-intermediate risk.

trials.name: ASCENDE-RT
trials.result: 9-y bPFS 83% vs 62%; more GU toxicity with boost
trials.takeaway: Brachytherapy boost improves biochemical control.

inclusion: Intermediate or high-risk localised prostate cancer
strengths: Improved biochemical control with LDR boost
appraisal.critique: Brachytherapy boost improves PSA control but at higher urinary toxicity cost.

trials.name: RADICALS-RT / RAVES / GETUG-AFU 17 (ARTISTIC)
trials.population: After radical prostatectomy with adverse features
arms: Early salvage RT on PSA rise
trials.result: No EFS benefit with adjuvant RT; early salvage avoided RT in ~half
trials.takeaway: Early salvage RT is preferred over routine adjuvant RT.

inclusion: After radical prostatectomy with adverse features (pT3/4, positive margins)
strengths: Meta-analysis showed early salvage equivalent to adjuvant RT
appraisal.critique: Early salvage RT is preferred; adjuvant RT for very high-risk features remains debated.

trials.name: STAMPEDE (arm H) M1 RT
trials.result: Low-volume: 3-y OS 81% vs 73% (HR 0.68); no benefit in high-volume
trials.takeaway: Prostate RT for low-volume mHSPC.

inclusion: Newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
strengths: OS benefit for low metastatic burden
limitations: Burden defined by CHAARTED criteria on conventional imaging
appraisal.critique: Prostate RT is standard for low-volume mHSPC.

trials.name: CHAARTED
trials.result: mOS 57.6 vs 44.0 mo; benefit in high-volume (HR 0.63)
trials.takeaway: Docetaxel with ADT for high-volume mHSPC.

appraisal.critique: Docetaxel benefit is clear in high-volume disease.

trials.name: LATITUDE / STAMPEDE abiraterone
trials.takeaway: Abiraterone with ADT for mHSPC.

appraisal.critique: Abiraterone is a standard addition to ADT; low-cost generics make it accessible in India.

trials.name: TITAN / ENZAMET / ARCHES
trials.result: TITAN OS HR 0.65; ENZAMET 5-y OS 67% vs 57%
trials.takeaway: ARPI intensification for all fit mHSPC patients.

appraisal.critique: ARPIs with ADT are standard regardless of volume.

trials.name: PEACE-1 / ARASENS
trials.result: ARASENS OS HR 0.68; PEACE-1 high-volume OS HR 0.72
trials.takeaway: Triplet therapy for fit high-volume de novo mHSPC.

appraisal.critique: Triplet therapy is an option for high-volume de novo disease.

trials.name: SPARTAN / PROSPER / ARAMIS
trials.population: nmCRPC with PSA doubling time ≤10 mo
trials.result: MFS gain ~2 years (HR ~0.3); OS benefit in all three
trials.takeaway: ARPI for high-risk nmCRPC.

inclusion: nmCRPC with PSA doubling time ≤10 months
limitations: PSMA-PET would reclassify many patients as metastatic
appraisal.critique: ARPIs are standard for high-risk nmCRPC, though PSMA-PET changes definitions.

trials.name: EMBARK
trials.takeaway: Combined enzalutamide + ADT for high-risk BCR.

inclusion: High-risk biochemical recurrence with PSADT ≤9 months
appraisal.critique: Enzalutamide + leuprolide is an option for high-risk BCR.

trials.name: TAX 327
trials.takeaway: First chemotherapy with survival benefit in mCRPC.

appraisal.critique: Docetaxel became the first chemotherapy to improve OS in mCRPC.

trials.name: COU-AA-301/302, AFFIRM, PREVAIL
trials.result: AFFIRM mOS 18.4 vs 13.6 mo; PREVAIL OS HR 0.71
trials.takeaway: ARPIs prolong survival in mCRPC.

appraisal.critique: ARPIs are standard; sequencing two ARPIs is less effective.

trials.name: TROPIC / CARD
trials.population: mCRPC after docetaxel (and an ARPI in CARD)
trials.takeaway: Cabazitaxel preferred over a second ARPI after docetaxel + ARPI.

inclusion: mCRPC after docetaxel (and an ARPI in CARD)
appraisal.critique: Cabazitaxel is preferred over a second ARPI after docetaxel and one ARPI.

trials.name: ALSYMPCA
trials.population: Symptomatic bone-metastatic CRPC, no visceral mets
trials.takeaway: Radium-223 for bone-predominant mCRPC (not with abiraterone).

appraisal.critique: Radium-223 is an option for bone-only disease.

trials.name: VISION
trials.population: PSMA-PET+ mCRPC after ARPI and taxane
trials.takeaway: Lu-PSMA is standard after ARPI and taxane in PSMA+ mCRPC.

appraisal.critique: Lu-PSMA is standard in later lines.

trials.name: PSMAfore
trials.population: Taxane-naive PSMA+ mCRPC after one ARPI
trials.takeaway: Lu-PSMA can be used before chemotherapy.

inclusion: Taxane-naive PSMA+ mCRPC after one ARPI
appraisal.critique: Lu-PSMA is an option before docetaxel.

trials.name: PROfound
trials.population: mCRPC with HRR alterations after ARPI
trials.result: Cohort A rPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 mo; OS 19.1 vs 14.7 mo
trials.takeaway: Test HRR genes; PARP inhibitor for BRCA-altered mCRPC.

inclusion: mCRPC with HRR alterations after ARPI
strengths: OS benefit in BRCA1/2, ATM cohort
appraisal.critique: Olaparib is standard for BRCA-mutated mCRPC.

trials.name: TALAPRO-2 / PROpel
trials.result: Greatest benefit in BRCA-mutated; TALAPRO-2 OS benefit reported
trials.takeaway: PARPi + ARPI first line, especially for HRR/BRCA-altered disease.

appraisal.critique: PARPi + ARPI is best for HRR-altered patients.

trials.name: SWOG 8710
trials.takeaway: Cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemo before cystectomy.

appraisal.critique: Established neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemo.

trials.name: VESPER
trials.takeaway: ddMVAC is a preferred neoadjuvant regimen.

appraisal.critique: ddMVAC is a preferred neoadjuvant option.

trials.name: NIAGARA
trials.takeaway: Perioperative durvalumab is a new standard for MIBC.

appraisal.critique: Perioperative durvalumab is a new standard.

trials.name: CheckMate 274
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab for high-risk resected urothelial cancer.

appraisal.critique: Adjuvant nivolumab is standard for high-risk resected MIUC.

trials.name: BC2001
trials.takeaway: Trimodality bladder preservation with concurrent 5-FU/MMC is standard.

appraisal.critique: Chemoradiotherapy with 5-FU/MMC is standard for bladder preservation.

trials.name: POUT
trials.population: Upper-tract urothelial carcinoma pT2–T4 or N+
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant platinum chemo after nephroureterectomy.

inclusion: Upper-tract urothelial carcinoma pT2–T4 or N+
appraisal.critique: Adjuvant chemotherapy is standard for UTUC.

trials.name: JAVELIN Bladder 100
trials.population: Advanced UC without progression after first-line platinum
